benchmark.name: LIBERO-PRO
benchmark.instruction_rule: task.language (from the file name); the swap leaves the instruction unchanged

tasks.instruction: pick up the alphabet soup and place it in the basket
pick up the bbq sauce and place it in the basket
pick up the butter and place it in the basket
pick up the chocolate pudding and place it in the basket
pick up the orange juice and place it in the basket

seeds.what_the_environment_seed_changes: The seed sets NumPy's global generator in the simulator process; it is set anew before every episode's reset. The start state then overwrites the joint positions and velocities of the scene. What the seed still decides is what the reset draws that is not part of that state: the benchmark places its fixtures (cabinet, stove, rack) at every reset within the ranges of the task's file, 1-2 cm. A fresh environment's first seeded reset always gives the same placement; a later reset of the same environment gives it in most tasks but not in all. So every reset's placement is compared with the scene's first, and the environment is built anew when it differs: every episode of a task starts from the same placement, whatever was run before it.

rollout.stop: the episode ends at the first step at which the predicate holds, or at the step limit
rollout.reset: environment seed, reset, start state, before every episode; the reset's placement of the fixtures is checked against the scene's first and the environment built anew when it differs
rollout.retry: none: an episode that raises is written with stopped = error and run again by the next launch

observation.image: uint8, as the simulator returns it, not flipped
observation.camera_parameters: intrinsics and extrinsics of both cameras at every query

endpoints.success: the BDDL goal of the task's file, checked after every policy step

parameters.close: the first policy step whose executed gripper command is > 0 after a command <= 0 (the gripper starts open)
parameters.close_is_on: the object or fixture owning the geom whose centre is nearest the gripper site at the frame after that step; every geom of every body of the entity counts
parameters.contact: the first policy step with a gripper geom in contact with a geom of an object or fixture
parameters.part: where the target names a part: the first contact with a body of the target's entity named like the target's body with another word in the part's place; the entity's other bodies (its frame) are skipped
parameters.reach_first_contact: the first entity touched is the target's entity and, where a part is named, the first part touched is the named one
parameters.entity_bodies: the bodies whose name is the entity's name or starts with it and an underscore; a body matching several entities belongs to the longest name

model.name: π0, the direct cut: the state token and the action tokens may not read the instruction

checkpoint.revision: none: the address has no revisions; the digest identifies the files

sha256.computed_as:
One digest for a checkpoint directory: sha256 over the lines '<file sha256>  ./<relative path>' of every
    file, sorted by path (`find . -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum`).

code.address: this repository, src/openpi (github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi at 15a9616 with reading annotations)

inference.images: main and wrist, each rotated by 180 degrees, resized with padding to 224 x 224, uint8; a third image slot, if the model has one, is masked
inference.state: end-effector position, axis-angle orientation, gripper joints (8 numbers), passed to openpi's transforms; read by the model as its configuration defines
inference.prompt: the instruction as given, tokenised by openpi's transforms
inference.precision: parameters restored as bfloat16 by openpi's create_trained_policy
inference.passes_per_query: 1 encoding of the images and the instruction; 1 action-expert evaluation at each Euler step; at the first query of an episode the row's checks add further passes, which do not enter the actions

settings.status: an instrument for the paper's pathway cuts (Sec. 3.3): one of the instruction's two ways to the action is cut; no row of the paper's tables
settings.image_tokens: the image tokens of every camera: every prefix position before the prompt
settings.action_side: the state token and the action tokens: every token the action expert computes
settings.instruction_is: every prompt position that holds a token, from <bos> to the closing newline, as the policy's own input transform tokenised this request
settings.how: attention masks passed to openpi's transformer; every layer and head, every Euler step of every query, for the whole episode; the model's velocity under the cut is integrated in every action dimension

checks.when: the first query of every episode, on its own observation and noise, in this process; a failed check stops the episode with an error
checks.tolerance: zero: every comparison is inside one process and has to hold bit for bit

measured.first_velocity: the arm's velocity at the first Euler step, [horizon, 7], as the model's velocity: the noise minus the sample after one Euler step of size 1 through the arm's program
measured.check_released: largest absolute difference between this instrument's chunk with nothing cut and the released policy's own program's chunk, same observation and noise; the episode stops unless they are equal bit for bit
measured.check_released_actions: largest absolute difference between the actions this row would execute from its chunk with nothing cut and the actions `Policy.infer` returns for the same request and noise; the episode stops unless they are equal bit for bit
measured.check_replaced_encoding: largest absolute difference between the arm's chunk and the arm's chunk with the instruction's keys and values replaced in the encoding; the episode stops unless they are equal bit for bit
measured.control_replaced_encoding: the same difference with nothing cut; the episode stops unless it is above zero

settings.recorded_per_query: first_velocity, check_released, check_released_actions, check_replaced_encoding, control_replaced_encoding; NaN at every query but the first of an episode

noise_seed_controls: The initial noise of every query, standard_normal((horizon, 32)) as float32 from numpy.random.default_rng(SeedSequence([noise seed, task index, start state, query index])): every episode of a unit has its own noise, rows on one model draw the same noise in the same episode, and an episode gets the same noise on any machine, in any order and under any sharding.
